answer: A sybil-resistant registry can throttle identity creation with escalating proof-of-work: every new agent must solve a puzzle whose difficulty rises automatically when registrations spike, like a nebula that thickens as more stars rush in. One honest agent pays a trivial cost, but an attacker minting thousands of fake identities faces a cost curve that climbs steeply with each extra account. Each solution is bound to one public key and threaded into an append-only log, so identities cannot be reused or resold, and the opal-like rarity of cheap early slots vanishes once abuse begins.
